title: The one-page policy
scenario:
You are the operations director at a home furniture retailer with 2,100 staff. Marketing uses an OpenAI API project for product copy. Customer service is piloting a Claude-based reply assistant. The company has a signed zero data retention (ZDR) arrangement with each vendor for its main organization.

The CEO wants a company AI policy approved this month. IT wrote a first draft. The exhibit shows it, with notes from your review.
exhibit:
AI policy: DRAFT v0.3 (made-up example data)

1. Tools    Staff may use approved AI tools for work.
2. Data     We have zero data retention with both vendors,
            so any customer data may go into any AI tool.
3. Review   Staff should use AI responsibly.
4. Access   All 14 developers have the admin role.
            API keys have no expiry date.
5. Reports  Problems: email ai-feedback@ (shared inbox)

Review notes
- Marketing created 3 new API projects last month.
  Retention setting on each: not checked.
- Customer service tests prompts in the vendor's
  web console (playground) with real customer emails.
- Planned use: the assistant drafts refund replies
  that agents send to customers.
- ai-feedback@ has 41 unread messages; no owner.

options.text: Nothing. A signed ZDR arrangement covers every project, product and model at that vendor.
options.explanation: The vendor docs say otherwise. OpenAI lets each project select "None", and the Claude docs list the Console and some models as not covered by ZDR.

options.text: It is too strict. Customer data is always safe with an API account, so no rule is needed.
options.explanation: API terms help, but they don't settle which settings apply to each project. The review notes show three projects nobody checked.

options.text: It assumes ZDR covers everything. It should name the settings and check each project and tool.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's data controls let a project inherit, change or turn off the retention control. Anthropic's docs list the Console playground as not covered by ZDR.

options.text: It should ban customer data from AI tools completely, since ZDR may change at any time.
options.explanation: A full ban blocks the customer service pilot, which needs customer emails. A rule tied to checked settings protects data and keeps the pilot.

questions.prompt: Rule 3 says "Staff should use AI responsibly." What should replace it?

options.text: A review rule per use, such as: a support lead approves each AI-drafted refund reply.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's safety guide recommends human review wherever possible, especially in high-stakes uses. A rule per use can be checked.

options.text: A rule that every AI output in the company, including internal notes, needs two reviewers first.
options.explanation: That is testable, but it treats a meeting note like a refund promise. Nobody can follow it, so people will ignore it.

options.text: No review rule, because a well-written prompt makes the assistant's refund replies correct.
options.explanation: Prompts help, but OpenAI's guide still recommends human review before outputs are used, especially when the stakes are high.

options.text: A line asking staff to watch a one-hour training video before their first use of any AI tool.
options.explanation: Training is useful, but it doesn't say who checks which output. The refund replies still go out unchecked.

options.text: Keep all 14 as admins, but ask them to be very careful with keys and settings.
options.explanation: "Be careful" is not testable. Anthropic's Admin API page advises regular audits of roles, which points to fewer admins, not more care.

options.text: Remove all API keys and let only the IT manager make AI calls for the whole company.
options.explanation: That stops the risk and also the work. The aim is the smallest role each person needs, not one person doing everything.

options.text: Give every developer a personal consumer account instead, so the company holds no keys.
options.explanation: That moves work to accounts the company doesn't control, with different data terms. It makes the policy weaker.

options.text: Give each person the smallest role they need, set key expiry, and audit roles often.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's Admin API page has separate developer and admin roles and advises regular role audits and key rotation. The OpenAI docs recommend key expiry and rotation.

questions.prompt: What is the main problem with rule 5 (Reports)?

options.text: Email is the wrong channel. Reports should only come through a chat bot.
options.explanation: OpenAI's safety guide names a listed email address as one acceptable method. The channel is fine; the missing owner is not.

options.text: Nobody owns the inbox. A named team should monitor reports and respond.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's safety guide says the reporting method should be monitored by a human and answered as appropriate. 41 unread messages show it isn't.

options.text: Reports are not needed once rule 3 has human review in place.
options.explanation: Review catches some problems before sending. Users still see problems that reviewers miss, so they need a way to report them.

options.text: Add an auto-reply to the inbox so senders know it was received.
options.explanation: An auto-reply is not a response. The guide says a human should monitor reports and respond.
